label: Marketing photoreal
description: Marketing design development within the measured envelope. The provider develops one shared architectural identity, subject to design-master approval and review of the complete set; publication quality is a target, not a certified result.
intent: Photorealistically finish this exact camera render into a publication-grade architectural photograph of the project. The result must read as a real photograph taken on site, not a render: real optics, real light transport, real material age.
allowed_changes: Develop an architect-designed, buildable industrial facade before photographing it. Respond to the actual building proportions and access: a coherent wall module, strong but restrained entrance hierarchy, deep reveals and shading where useful, a durable base and clean roof-edge resolution. Offices should read as human-scale working spaces, not an oversized glass showroom; logistics doors remain practical and accessible. Replace arbitrary procedural stripes, repeated red fins and generic feature frames with one disciplined site-specific composition. Use the client accent sparingly rather than decorating every bay. Establish this design in the Design Master and repeat it consistently, never independently redesigning each image. Resolve real metal, concrete and glass with joints, fixings, restrained weathering and realistic reflections. Keep entourage modest, correctly scaled and outside architecture and access paths; develop planting only within authored zones. Preserve measured massing, continuous roofs and functional openings.
photography: Full-frame architectural photography with a perspective-corrected lens. Physically plausible daylight for the stated time of day, neutral white balance, highlight roll-off that holds detail in bright metal roofing, and shadows that retain colour rather than crushing to black. Sharp across the subject with natural lens falloff. Corrugated and profiled metal must show fine seams, real fixings and shallow surface waviness, never smooth plastic planes. Concrete and asphalt must show aggregate, joints, drainage falls, tyre marks and restrained operational wear. The image should be good enough to publish as the project's lead marketing photograph.
context_direction: The estate around the project is real and recently built: sealed roads with kerbs and line marking, neighbouring lots with their own hardstanding and sheds, boundary fences, verges, service infrastructure and mature planting, continuing to a hazy industrial horizon. Resolve every flat or translucent placeholder volume into a believable neighbouring building; never let a grey slab survive into the final image. Keep the surroundings clearly secondary to the project.
prohibited: No fantasy colour, no surreal lighting, no impossible structure.
